[[File:Tulipa sylvestris MHNT.BOT.2015.34.30.jpg|thumb|''Tulipa sylvestris'' - [[MHNT]]]]

'''''Tulipa sylvestris''''', the '''wild tulip'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=TUSY|taxon=Tulipa sylvestris|accessdate=12 December 2015}}</ref> or  '''woodland tulip''',<ref name="perennialmeadows">{{cite web|url=http://www.perennialmeadows.com/2013/05/tulipa-sylvestris-the-woodland-tulip/ |title=Perennial Meadows, Design & Plant, Tulipa sylvestris – the woodland tulip |date=16 May 2013 |publisher=perennialmeadows.com|accessdate=2015-05-02}}</ref> is a [[Eurasia]]n and [[North Africa]]n species of wild [[tulip]], a plant in the [[Liliaceae|lily family]]. Its native range extends from [[Portugal]] and [[Morocco]] to western [[China]], covering most of the [[Mediterranean Basin|Mediterranean]] and [[Black Sea]] Basins, and [[Central Asia]]. The species is also cultivated as an ornamental and naturalized in central and northern Europe as well as a few scattered locations in [[North America]].<ref name=wilma/><ref name="usda">{{cite web|url=http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=TUSY |title=Plants Profile for Tulipa sylvestris (wild tulip) | United States Department of Agriculture plants profile |publisher=plants.usda.gov|access-date=2015-05-02}}</ref> 
It was first recorded as being naturalised in Britain in the late 17th century.<ref name="Cuttle">{{cite book |last1=Spencer-Jones |first1=Rae |last2=Cuttle |first2=Sarah |title=Wild Flowers of Britain and Ireland |date=2005 |publisher=Kyle Cathie Limited |location=London |isbn=9781856265034 |page=80}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Tulipa sylvestris 130405.jpg|thumb|''Tulipa sylvestris'']]
It is a bulb-forming perennial, with narrow blue-grey leaves and usually with 1 or 2 flowers per stem.<ref name="Cuttle"/> The stem can reach up to {{cvt|50|cm}} tall. The scented blooms appear between April and May,<ref name="Cuttle"/> and the yellow flowers are sometimes tinged red on the outside.<ref name="altervista">{{cite web|url=http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=tulipa+australis |title=Altervista Flora Italiana, Tulipano selvatico, ''Tulipa australis'' Link |publisher=luirig.altervista.org|accessdate=2015-05-02}}</ref><ref name="bonap">{{cite web|url=http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Tulipa%20sylvestris.png |title= Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map |publisher=bonap.net|accessdate=2015-05-02}}</ref><ref>Everett, D. (2013). The genus ''Tulipa'' Tulips of the world: 1-380. Kew publishing, Kew.</ref><ref>Christenhusz, M.J.M., Govaerts, R., David, J.C., Hall, T., Borland, K., Roberts, P.S., Tuomisto, A., Buerki, S., Chase, M.W. & Fay, M.F. (2013). Tiptoe through the tulips - cultural history, molecular phylogenetics and classification of Tulipa (Liliaceae). Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society 172: 280-328.</ref>

They rarely produce seed and are [[pollination|pollinated]] by small insects.<ref name="Cuttle"/>

=== Biochemicals ===
Some [[tuliposides]] – a family of biochemicals – found in ''Tulipa sylvestris'' include:<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Christensen |first=L |date=August 1999 |title=Tuliposides from Tulipa sylvestris and T. turkestanica |url=https://doi.org/10.1016/S0031-9422(98)00716-X |journal=Phytochemistry |volume=51 |issue=8 |pages=969–974 |doi=10.1016/s0031-9422(98)00716-x |bibcode=1999PChem..51..969C |issn=0031-9422|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

* 6-tuliposide A and B
* Tuliposide D
* Tulipalin A and B

=== Subspecies ===
There are three ''T. sylvestris'' subspecies:

* ''Tulipa sylvestris'' subsp. ''australis'' {{small|((Link) Pamp)}} – from [[Portugal]] and [[Morocco]] to [[Xinjiang]]<ref name="wilma" />
* ''Tulipa sylvestris'' subsp. ''primulina'' {{small|((Baker) Maire & Weiller)}} – [[Algeria]], [[Morocco]]<ref name="wilma" />
* ''Tulipa sylvestris'' subsp. ''sylvestris'' – [[Italy]], [[Libya]]<ref name="wilma" />

''Tulipa australis'' is also found on the [[Malta (island)|island of Malta]], in the [[Mediterranean Sea]], limited to one specific area.<ref name="schembri">{{cite book|last1=Schembri|first1=Patrick J.|last2=Baldacchino|first2=Alfred E.|title=Ilma, Blat u Hajja: Is-Sisien tal-Ambjent Naturali Malti|language=Maltese|url=http://www.bdlbooks.com/geography/3394-ilma-blat-u-hajja.html|isbn=978-99909-44-48-8|date=2011|page=81|publisher=Malta University Press }}</ref>

==Habitat==
It is found in dry grassy places and in woodland copses.<ref name="Cuttle"/>
